Subject: Integrator concierge — SDK & migration support request

Hi Sergio / Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. BlueHarbor is aiming to migrate our internal document-generation flow to Redwood for inference. Our target cutover is around June 1; before that we need: a ready-to-drop SDK snippet pack, a recommended throttling map for our expected traffic profile, and a short migration runbook we can follow for staging -> prod.

A few constraints on our side:
- Production traffic expected ~120 TPS peak to /v1/generate with bursts up to 300 TPS for ~30s.
- Average request length ~220 tokens, some long-tail up to 1,200 tokens.
- We need guidance on client-side retries/timeouts to avoid double-charging or long tail latency.

Can you share:
1) Node + Python sample code with sensible default timeouts and retry/backoff (we use axios and requests stacks).
2) Suggested per-endpoint rate limits (burst/steady) and a simple client-side token-bucket example.
3) A short sequence of staging checks for endpoint migration and rollback criteria.

If possible, please send the artifacts as a single bundle; we can schedule a 30-min kickoff next week once we have the pack.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Senior Platform Engineer
BlueHarbor Integrations

Alyssa

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Integrator concierge — throttle map excerpt & client token-bucket example

A quick technical addendum from the runtime side:

Excerpt from throttle-map-v2.csv:
endpoint, steady_tps, burst_tps, notes
/v1/generate, 120, 320, recommend per-customer burst bucket + global guard
/v1/embeddings, 40, 100, embeddings are heavier for long sequences
/v1/health, 60, 60, low-cost heartbeat route

Client-side token-bucket (pseudo):
- bucket_capacity = 400  # tokens
- refill_rate = 120 tokens/sec  # steady
- On each request: if tokens >= cost(tokens_of_request) then consume and send, else queue/fast-fail depending on SLAs.

Backoff guidance (summary):
- For bursts, prefer client-side queuing + jittered backoff before retries to avoid thundering herd.
- For long-tail requests (>1k tokens): set a higher per-request token cost and a longer max timeout (60s) but do not retry automatically. Instead, surface these calls to a separate queue and instrument separately.

Small curl example to show 'Retry-After' handling (server returns 429 with Retry-After in seconds):

#!/bin/bash
RETRIES=0
MAX=3
while [ $RETRIES -le $MAX ]
do
  HTTP=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate)
  if [ "$HTTP" = "200" ]; then break; fi
  if [ "$HTTP" = "429" ]; then
    RA=$(curl -s -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep -i Retry-After | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\r')
    SLEEP=${RA:-1}
    sleep $SLEEP
  else
    sleep $((2 ** $RETRIES))
  fi
  RETRIES=$((RETRIES+1))
done

I uploaded the CSV and included a small visualization in the Drive link so your traffic team can toy with the steady/burst numbers.

Subject: Re: Integrator concierge — migration runbook and timeline

Hi Alyssa team — I put together the migration-runbook-v1.pdf with a concise rollout plan. High-level steps:

1) Pre-cutover (2 weeks)
   - Provision a dedicated staging project and mirror traffic using 5% shadowing of prod queries.
   - Run 48-hour stress window at 2x expected steady to validate autoscaling and KV cache warmup.
   - Validate token costs and telemetry hooks (latency, retry count, 429s).

2) Cutover day (T-0)
   - Warm caches via traffic replay (30 minutes).
   - Soft-cut: route 10% for 30 minutes, monitor error rate (<0.5%), p95 latency, and token burn.
   - If metrics good -> 50% for 45 minutes -> 100% for final flip.

3) Rollback criteria
   - Sustained error rate >1% for 15 minutes, or p95 latency >2x baseline for 30 minutes, or unexpected token burn >20% of estimate.
   - Rollback: flip routing to previous endpoint, inform stakeholders, and initiate post-mortem.

4) Post-cutover (first 72 hours)
   - Elevated monitoring: hourly check-ins for first 6 hours, then 4-hour cadence up to 72 hours.

I'll also add a small checklist for infra engineers: update client SDK keys, confirm DNS TTLs (we recommend 60s), and validate observability dashboards. See runbook in Drive.

Proposed attendees for the kickoff: Alyssa, Timothy (BlueHarbor infra), Sergio (CSM), Vanessa (SSE), Vivek (Runtime eng), Monica (Impl lead).

Happy to walk through the runbook during the kickoff and annotate any BlueHarbor-specific steps.

- Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
